Given an invertible $n\times n$ matrix $A,$ we have

$$
det({A}^{-1})=\frac{1}{det(A)}.
$$

First, we find $det(A):$

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A) & =det[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 \\ 4 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =-6-4 \\  & =-10\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain 

$$
det({A}^{-1})=\frac{1}{det(A)}=-\frac{1}{10}.
$$

Therefore, we obtain 

$$

questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that the $2$nd row of our determinant is almost equal to the $3$rd row. So, we can rewrite the given determinant, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 6 \\ 91 & 92 & 93 \\ 90 & 92 & 93\end{aligned}| & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 6 \\ 90+1 & 92+0 & 93+0 \\ 90 & 92 & 93\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}
$$

Next, using the linearity property of determinants, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 6 \\ 90+1 & 92+0 & 93+0 \\ 90 & 92 & 93\end{aligned}| & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 6 \\ 90 & 92 & 93 \\ 90 & 92 & 93\end{aligned}|+|\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 6 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 90 & 92 & 93\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

The first determinant must be zero since it has two identical rows, while the second determinant can be expanded across the $2$nd row, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 6 \\ 90 & 92 & 93 \\ 90 & 92 & 93\end{aligned}|+|\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 6 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 90 & 92 & 93\end{aligned}| & =0+1(-1)^{2+1}|\begin{aligned}3 & 6 \\ 92 & 93\end{aligned}| \\  & =-(3\cdot 93-6\cdot 92) \\  & =-(279-552) \\  & =273\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
Given an invertible $n\times n$ matrix $A,$ we have

$$
|{A}^{-1}|=\frac{1}{|A|}.
$$

First, we find $|A|$ using a Laplace expansion across the $2$nd row:

$$
\begin{aligned}|A| & =|\begin{aligned}-5 & -3 & 4 \\ -2 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & -4 & 6\end{aligned}| \\  & =-2(-1)^{2+1}|\begin{aligned}-3 & 4 \\ -4 & 6\end{aligned}|+1(-1)^{2+2}|\begin{aligned}-5 & 4 \\ 1 & 6\end{aligned}|+2(-1)^{2+3}|\begin{aligned}-5 & -3 \\ 1 & -4\end{aligned}| \\  & =2(-18+16)+(-30-4)-2(20+3) \\  & =-4-34-46 \\  & =-84\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain 

$$
|{A}^{-1}|=\frac{1}{|A|}=-\frac{1}{84}.
$$

We "factor out" the given determinant from the determinant we would like to find:

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}a+4 & 5 \\ b+2 & -3\end{aligned}| & =|\begin{aligned}(a+5)-1 & 5 \\ b+2 & -3\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using the linearity property of determinants, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}(a+5)-1 & 5 \\ b+2 & -3\end{aligned}| & ={{|\begin{aligned}a+5 & 5 \\ b & -3\end{aligned}|}_{⏟}}_{-34}+|\begin{aligned}-1 & 5 \\ 2 & -3\end{aligned}| \\  & =-34+(3-10) \\  & =-41.\end{aligned}
$$
